methods.label: Use the inverse relationship between speed and time
methods.explanation:
For a fixed distance, speed multiplied by time stays constant. Thus taking \(\tfrac45\) as much time requires \(\tfrac54\) as much speed. The increase of \(\tfrac12\) mile per hour is therefore one-fourth of the original speed, so the original speed was
\[
\frac{1/2}{1/4}=2\text{ miles per hour}.
\]
The slower speed would have been \(2-\tfrac12=\tfrac32\) miles per hour, which is \(\tfrac34\) of the original speed. It would therefore require \(\tfrac43\) of the original time. The extra time is one-third of the original time, and that extra time is \(2\tfrac12\) hours. Hence the original time was
\[
\frac{5/2}{1/3}=\frac{15}{2}\text{ hours}.
\]
Both hypothetical speeds are positive, as required for walking the distance. Finally, distance equals speed multiplied by time, giving
\[
2\cdot\frac{15}{2}=15\text{ miles},
\]
choice B.
